check.name: lens.design
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

message.text: `MissEvidence.stagesAt` used to keep every `melian.lens` stage whose coverage held the miss's file. It now calls `MissLines.covers`, and the fix pass added `stage.role !== "prober"` to that method so `MissCause` and `Miss.unscoped` would agree. That edit also reached the evidence store, so a prober's conversation is no longer kept as evidence for a valid miss.

evidence.snippet: 2. The evidence is the round's lens conversations whose coverage holds the miss's file, the verifier conversations whose claims include a lens sighting overlapping the miss's lines, every entry of each, and the round's base, head and policy commits, with the blob IDs of the lens files at the policy commit. A miss with no file and line, one the comparison marks outdated, or one on the base keeps the commits and no conversation, since no lens's coverage or sighting can be matched to it. Deciding whether a lens saw the lines, and naming the cause, is later work.

explanation.what: `MissEvidence.stagesAt` used to keep every `melian.lens` stage whose coverage held the miss's file. It now calls `MissLines.covers`, and the fix pass added `stage.role !== "prober"` to that method so `MissCause` and `Miss.unscoped` would agree. That edit also reached the evidence store, so a prober's conversation is no longer kept as evidence for a valid miss.
explanation.whatToDo: Keep the prober filter out of what `stagesAt` keeps. One option is to leave `covers` as a pure coverage test and apply the prober exclusion only in `MissCause` and `Miss.unscoped`. Another is to give `stagesAt` its own coverage predicate that keeps probers. Then add an evidence test where a prober stage with coverage of the file is kept.
explanation.whyHere: The base decision 'A valid miss keeps the conversations behind it', item 2, says the evidence is "the round's lens conversations whose coverage holds the miss's file". It also says that deciding whether a lens saw the lines is later work. A prober is a lens conversation: `lensPolicy` gives it the lens's coverage, and `spawnProber` gives it the lens's read tools and `report_finding`. At a level that probes, the prober is the conversation that reports. Evidence is copied once, when the miss is adjudicated. Once a later round replaces the telemetry, a conversation left out can never be recovered, and that loss is what the decision exists to prevent. The progress log says the prober check was moved so that 'both callers share it', but `stagesAt` is a third caller, and no decision text was changed to allow narrowing the evidence.

properties.failureScenario: Take one of Melian's own rounds at deep, where probing is on and `trust-boundary-probes` runs a planner and a prober. Both stages are `melian.lens` and both carry the lens's coverage. Codex flags `src/user.ts:30`, and the maintainer runs `melian compare adjudicate ... --verdict valid`. `MissEvidence.gather` calls `stagesAt`. At base, both the planner's and the prober's conversations were written under `evidence/<changeset>/<round>/stages/`. At head, `lines.covers(prober)` returns false because of `role !== "prober"`, so only the planner's conversation is kept. The planner was told it reports nothing at this level. The prober is the conversation that ran probes, read the file and could have reported, and it is silently dropped. After the next round replaces the telemetry, `melian compare evidence` cannot show what the prober did, so nobody can tell why the probing level missed the defect.
